observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³. Laboratory stability KV ≳ 25 kT gives V ≈ 2.3e-26 m³ (~30 nm linear) at 300 K. Magnetite blocking size is a 10–30 nm class for near-equant grains, not a single cliff.
implied_text: The latch hardware is unchanged from the parent magnet. Below the stability volume the barrier is under-provisioned by grain size, not by a missing anisotropy mechanism.
description: The spatial-buffer clause of the magnetic latch is a crystalline anisotropy cell at tens of nanometres for NdFeB at laboratory time.
value_text: V ≳ 2.3e-26 m³ (~30 nm NdFeB); KV ≳ 25 kT
notes: 25 kT is a timescale convention, not a single experimental cliff. Magnetite has no single portable diameter.

observed_text: Néel–Arrhenius attempt time τ0 is empirically 10^{-10}–10^{-12} s. Thermal escape attempts run on that scale (~10^{-11} s).
implied_text: In a stable grain the attempts bounce off the barrier. In an under-volume grain they succeed inside τm and rewrite the directional state at random.
description: The failure clock of the latch is the Néel attempt time, not the 28 GHz/T precession carrier.
notes: Single-spin precession remains ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}; that carrier is not the failure clock.

observed_text: Uniaxial barrier ΔE ≈ K1 V. Nd2Fe14B K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³. Superparamagnetism is that barrier times an insufficient V, compared with kT ln(τm/τ0).
implied_text: This is not a different barrier from the permanent-magnet latch. Collapse is under-provisioned volume at fixed K and T.
description: The same KV barrier holds a bulk grain and fails a nanoparticle; only V has changed.
notes: Cubic magnetite |K1| ≈ 1.35e4 J/m³; do not substitute |K1|V as if it were the uniaxial barrier. Shape anisotropy can dominate Keff in non-equant grains.

observed_text: KV ≲ kT ln(τm/τ0) (laboratory convention KV ≲ 25 kT) → remanence and coercivity collapse to zero; M(H) is reversible and Langevin-like.
implied_text: Thermal erasure of the directional latch on the observation window. Spatial-buffer twin of the thin-film mirror.
description: Too-small grains erase the latch on the observer's clock without reaching Tc.
value_text: KV ≲ 25 kT (~30 nm NdFeB lab window)
notes: Recording uses a 40–60 kT convention; Mössbauer windows sit near 10^{-8} s. Same contour, different clocks. T > Tc is the parent Curie collapse, not this volume cliff.

observed_text: On the unblocked side, coercivity and remanence collapse to zero; M(H) is reversible and Langevin-like. A blocking contour TB(V, τm) recovers the loop below it.
implied_text: Stable unblocked output is a zero-remanence ensemble curve plus the blocking surface, not a motor moment.
description: The unblocked grain emits a reversible Langevin curve and a blocking contour, not a usable remanent force.
notes: A single unblocked grain’s fluctuating moment is not a usable motor; the Langevin curve is already an ensemble average. Blocked side is the parent latch.

observed_text: Holding the unblocked state costs no continuous power; the directional memory is simply gone. Zero continuous power on the blocked side as well.
implied_text: Neither the fluctuating unblocked ensemble nor the blocked parent latch draws hold power.
description: Holding either side of the blocking contour costs zero watts.

observed_text: Real coercivity is not Ha, and real K of a nanoparticle is not the bulk K1. Surface anisotropy, grain-boundary structure, and dipolar coupling sit between unit-cell anisotropy and observed TB.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale Keff step.
description: The volume-and-time collapse does not depend on closing nanoparticle Keff; the mesoscale step remains underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Brownian relaxation in a fluid is a different machine and is not this entry.

observed_text: A remanent branch requires a grain with KV above the Néel–Arrhenius laboratory line, embedded in a lattice that supplies K. Soft matrices supply order (high Tc) without a usable write barrier.
implied_text: Minimum hardware is a thermally stable anisotropy cell. The loop as a macroscopic object further requires a readable population — grain ensemble, domain pattern, or bulk body.
description: A single spin has no useful remanence against kT; the loop needs a latched grain plus a readable aligned population.
value_text: grain with KV above the thermal line; no single loop N
notes: Volume cliff owned in detail by superparamagnetism. Soft/hard split is the barrier, not Tc.

observed_text: Larmor / FMR scale: γ/2π ≈ 28.025 GHz/T. Practical loop traversal is set by the field sweep and by domain-wall motion (and, in metals, eddy currents), not by that carrier.
implied_text: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession clock; write/erase latency of a real loop is a slower, microstructure-limited wall-motion clock.
description: Holding remanence does not run the 28 GHz/T carrier as a power draw; writing the loop does not finish on that carrier either.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency.

observed_text: Uniaxial anisotropy density K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³ for Nd2Fe14B; μ0 Ha ≈ 7–8 T. Energy per unit volume per cycle equals the loop area ∮H·dB. Holding a static remanent point costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: The barrier that protects remanence is the same anisotropy barrier as the permanent-magnet latch. Energy is spent only to write and erase.
description: Hysteresis is the write/erase cycle of the anisotropy latch: zero hold-power plus finite loop-area cost.
notes: The operating write field is Hc, much smaller than Ha in almost all bulk magnets. That mesoscale step is the §4.6 gap.

observed_text: Soft iron and silicon steel: coercivity typically < 10^2–10^3 A/m. Remanence exists but is not stable against ordinary self-demagnetizing fields.
implied_text: Barrier / pinning too small → Hc → 0, loop area → 0 → remanence does not survive removal of H. The metal may still be ferromagnetic.
description: The soft-limit collapse is loss of the write barrier, not loss of ferromagnetic order.
notes: Iron Tc ≈ 1043 K: still ferromagnetic, just not latched. Contrast sintered NdFeB tesla-class μ0 Hc ≪ Ha ~ 7–8 T.

observed_text: Iron Tc ≈ 1043 K; Nd2Fe14B Tc ≈ 585 K. Above Tc the ordered moment is gone and the loop disappears.
implied_text: Thermal destruction of the ordered moment removes the loop. This is not the soft-limit or the volume cliff.
description: No ordered moment above Tc, so no remanent branch and no hysteresis loop.
value_text: T > Tc (585 K Nd2Fe14B; 1043 K Fe)
notes: value_si is the NdFeB handbook cliff used on the parent latch. KV ≲ 25 kT is the volume twin, filed as superparamagnetism.

observed_text: After a large field is removed, a remanent magnetization remains. Energy per unit volume per cycle equals the loop area ∮H·dB.
implied_text: Stable output is remanence at H = 0 plus a finite write/erase energy equal to the loop area.
description: The loop is the latch cycle: remanent state at zero field, dissipative cost only when the state is written.
value_text: Mr at H = 0; w = ∮H·dB per cycle

observed_text: A sample sitting at rest on a remanent branch produces no continuous hysteresis heat. Holding a static remanent point costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Zero hold power plus finite loop-area write cost is the latch accounting.
description: Holding either remanent branch costs zero watts. Energy is the write/erase loop area only.

observed_text: Sintered NdFeB coercivity is typically tesla-class (often ~1 T in μ0 Hc), much less than μ0 Ha ≈ 7–8 T. Stoner–Wohlfarth coherent rotation predicts a switching field of order Ha.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a buffer/barrier specification that produces Hc from nucleation, grain boundaries, dipolar coupling, and wall pinning.
description: Measured Hc is a mesoscale write threshold, not Ha. Soft-limit, Tc, and zero-hold-power clauses do not depend on closing it.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. ~1 T is a class, not a grade-specific number.

observed_text: Small grains and ultrathin films lose stable remanence (superparaelectric / depolarization collapse). A single laboratory-stability volume is not claimed; depolarization fields and electrodes enter.
implied_text: Hardware is a polar lattice cell plus a correlated volume large enough that the polar well survives kT and the depolarization field. Ceramic remanence is synchronized output of a poled grain population.
description: One unit-cell dipole is not a macroscopic remanent capacitor; the grain/thickness buffer is real as a class and has no portable number here.
notes: Do not import KV ≳ 25 kT as a ferroelectric constant.

observed_text: The polar displacement is ionic and sits on the lattice-mode clock (optical-phonon / THz class). Macroscopic switching of a ceramic or a multidomain crystal is set by nucleation and wall motion under applied E.
implied_text: The latch carrier is the ionic/phonon clock; ceramic write latency is a slower wall-motion clock.
description: Polar switching does not finish on the phonon period in a real ceramic; the THz class is the local displacement clock.
notes: No numerical phonon frequency is given in the file.

observed_text: A polar double well, locked to a non-centrosymmetric lattice, holds ±Pr at E = 0. Holding remanent P at E = 0 costs zero continuous power. Energy per cycle is ∮E·dP.
implied_text: The latch is the polar well. Energy is spent only on transitions. The write threshold is Ec, not the Landau barrier of a perfect crystal.
description: Remanent polarity is protected by a lattice-locked double well at zero hold-power; write cost is the P–E loop area.
value_text: double well below Tc; write at Ec
notes: Ec of bulk BaTiO3 and PZT-family ceramics is kV cm^{-1} class; the class, not a grade-specific number, is the boundary.

observed_text: BaTiO3 Tc ≈ 120 °C (393 K). Above Tc the room-temperature tetragonal polar phase is gone and remanent P collapses. End-member PbTiO3 Tc ≈ 490 °C.
implied_text: kT closing the polar well destroys the latch. Further BaTiO3 polar-phase changes (~5 °C, −90 °C) are structure changes of an already-latched state.
description: Thermal collapse of the polar latch at the ferroelectric Curie point.
notes: PZT family is composition-dependent; no single PZT Tc is claimed. value_si is the BaTiO3 handbook cliff.

observed_text: Small grains and ultrathin films lose stable remanence. Depolarization field of a uniformly polarized slab is of order P/ε, reduced by electrodes and free charge.
implied_text: Spatial / electrostatic under-provisioning makes P volatile. This is the electrical analog of superparamagnetism, not a portable KV line.
description: Too-small or uncompensated polar volumes erase remanence without reaching Tc.
notes: Dielectric breakdown at larger E is hardware failure of the insulator, not a clean rewrite.

observed_text: Room-temperature spontaneous polarization of single-crystal BaTiO3 along c is Ps ≈ 0.26 C/m². Ceramic remanence is lower; PZT-family Pr remains in the 10^{-1} C/m² class.
implied_text: Stable output is remanent polarization and the associated bound charge / field at E = 0.
description: The polar latch emits a material-typical remanent P, not a linear dielectric that returns to P = 0.
value_text: Ps ≈ 0.26 C m^{-2} (BaTiO3); Pr ~ 10^{-1} C m^{-2} class

observed_text: The sample remains electrically poled at zero continuous field and zero continuous power. Holding remanent P at E = 0 costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Stable remanent polarization and bound charge / field at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / grain / electrode / lattice envelope.
description: Holding remanent polarity costs zero watts. Energy is the P–E loop area only.

observed_text: Ec is microstructure- and thickness-dependent. The superparaelectric size line is not a portable KV/25kT constant: depolarization, screening, and electrodes are extra constraints.
implied_text: QSA does not derive Ec from the Landau well, nor a laboratory-stability volume from node rules.
description: Write threshold and grain/depolarization buffer remain mesoscale data without a closed QSA specification.
value_text: Ec mesoscale; no portable ferroelectric KV
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. kV cm^{-1} class is taken, not derived.

observed_text: Two-sublattice accounting: MA ≈ −MB, so Mnet ≈ 0. Each sublattice magnetization is of ordinary atomic-moment size. A single spin is not an antiferromagnet.
implied_text: Hardware is two (or more) interpenetrating sublattices, each a directional latch, correlated over a volume large enough that exchange holds the antiparallel relation against kT.
description: The cancelled latch requires at least two opposed ordered populations, not a single-moment cell.
notes: Readable hardware is the magnetic superlattice (neutron / resonant x-ray / AFM-resonance), not a dipole field. Finite-size reduction of TN is noted without a portable KV.

observed_text: The protecting energy is exchange, set by kTN. The corresponding rate is far above ordinary ferromagnetic FMR.
implied_text: There is no slow AFM write unless a spin-flop field or an exchange-bias field-cool is imposed. Macroscopic readout of the cancelled moment is not a hysteresis clock.
description: Exchange, not the 28 GHz/T ferromagnetic carrier, sets the AFM protecting rate.
value_text: exchange rate ≫ FMR; set by kTN
notes: No numerical AFM resonance frequency is given in the file.

observed_text: Exchange locks each sublattice against the other. Holding the ordered (cancelled) state costs zero continuous power. Mean-field TN ~ J identifies the exchange energy with the thermal cliff.
implied_text: The barrier is inter-sublattice exchange. The emergent dipole is ~0 because the two latches are opposed; cancelled force is the output, not a failure.
description: A latch is a held configuration at zero hold-power, not a requirement of a nonzero dipole.
notes: TN ~ J is a fit to the thermal cliff, not a derivation of J from a node rule.

observed_text: Handbook Néel points of the rock-salt monoxide class: MnO TN ≈ 118 K; FeO TN ≈ 198 K; NiO TN ≈ 523 K. Above TN the superlattice intensity is gone and the material is an ordinary paramagnet.
implied_text: Thermal over-barrier collapse of both sublattices → magnetic Bragg gone, Curie–Weiss paramagnet.
description: The cancelled latch dies at TN, the analog of a ferromagnetic Curie point.
notes: FeO is stoichiometry-sensitive. These are measured collapse temperatures of Bragg intensity and the susceptibility cusp.

observed_text: Ordinary applied fields (well below a spin-flop / spin-flip field) do not rewrite AFM order into a net ferromagnet. Spin-flop fields, where measured, are tesla-class or larger in the monoxides.
implied_text: A spin-flop field is a field write of the AFM configuration, not everyday ferromagnetic coercivity. Ordinary laboratory H is usually under that threshold.
description: Tesla-class fields can rewrite the relative sublattice orientation; ordinary lab fields do not make a permanent magnet.
notes: A given crystal’s spin-flop field is medium (anisotropy- and sample-dependent). No named-compound field is quoted.

observed_text: Mnet ≈ 0 on the scale of a ferromagnet of the same sublattice magnetization. The sample exerts no useful permanent-magnet force.
implied_text: Cancelled net moment / ~0 force is the stable output of two opposed latches, not evidence that nothing is latched.
description: The cancelled latch emits approximately zero macroscopic force while the neutron superlattice remains.
notes: Weak canting in some compounds is a parasitic remainder; it does not convert the family into the permanent-magnet latch.

observed_text: Holding the ordered (cancelled) state costs zero continuous power. There is no hysteresis-heat bill at rest.
implied_text: A static antiparallel superlattice with Mnet ≈ 0, held at zero continuous power below TN.
description: Holding the cancelled latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: The mapping takes the sign of the inter-sublattice coupling as data (the lattice and electronic structure that make J antiferromagnetic).
implied_text: QSA does not here derive why MnO is AFM and Fe is FM. That is a gap in the node rules, not a gap in the latch accounting.
description: The AFM sign of J is taken, not produced from a more primitive node rule.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Weak ferromagnetism/canting is not this gap.

observed_text: Hex falls as the FM layer is made thicker, empirically close to 1/tFM over a working window. Too thin an AFM layer also kills the shift. There is no exchange-bias loop in a separated AFM and FM of the same materials.
implied_text: Hardware is an AFM volume that stays blocked, an FM film thin enough that the interface pin is not diluted below a usable Hex, and a shared interface.
description: Two nested latches plus an interface; missing any of the three removes the shift.
value_text: AFM pin + FM film + interface; Hex ~ 1/t_FM
notes: No numerical working thickness is given in the file.

observed_text: Setting the pin is a thermal write: the field-cool must pass through TB on a laboratory cooling clock. Subsequent FM writes are ordinary hysteresis clocks on an already-offset loop.
implied_text: The pin is set slowly by cooling through the AFM blocking contour. AFM exchange rates underneath are fast compared with either the cool or the FM sweep.
description: Pin-setting latency is a laboratory field-cool through TB; no numerical cool time is specified.
notes: Training (first loops after field-cooling differ) is recorded as pin relaxation without a node-level clock.

observed_text: The FM loop is centered at −Hex. Switching thresholds sit near −Hex ± Hc, not at ±Hc. Hex is the field equivalent of the pin; Hc is still the half-width of the FM cycle.
implied_text: The AFM cancelled latch leaves a unidirectional barrier on the FM at the interface. That offset holds at zero continuous power. The FM still has its own bidirectional anisotropy barrier.
description: Exchange bias is a second, unidirectional latch stacked on the FM cycle, not a replacement for Hc.
value_text: H_ex (loop offset); H_c still the half-width
notes: Meiklejohn–Bean Hex ≈ Jex/(μ0 Ms tFM); Jex is an effective interface energy density, not bulk AFM exchange.

observed_text: Hex → 0 as T → TB−. TB ≤ TN of the AFM. TB tracks AFM thickness and grain size and can lie well below the bulk Néel point.
implied_text: Thermal unblocking of the pin removes the shift and leaves a centered FM loop. The FM may still be ordered (its Tc is a different cliff).
description: The pin dies at TB, which is not a second name for TN.
notes: No numerical TB is given for a named stack.

observed_text: Hex falls as the FM layer is made thicker, empirically close to 1/tFM. Too thin an AFM layer also kills the shift (the pin itself is under-provisioned).
implied_text: FM-side buffer dilution and AFM-side under-provisioning are the two spatial failures of the nested latch.
description: Too thick an FM film dilutes Hex; too thin an AFM film unblocks the pin.
value_text: H_ex ~ 1/t_FM; AFM too thin → no pin
notes: Chemical / mechanical destruction of the interface is a third buffer failure.

observed_text: The hysteresis loop is shifted along the field axis rather than centered at H = 0. The shift is Hex, opposite the cooling field in the usual convention.
implied_text: Stable output is an offset −Hex of the FM loop and a remanent FM state whose zero-field point is no longer symmetric.
description: The machine emits a unidirectional loop offset, not a centered remanence.
notes: An increase of FM coercivity often accompanies the shift; the two numbers are not the same artifact.

observed_text: Holding the shifted remanent point costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent to field-cool (set the pin) and to traverse the shifted loop (write the FM).
implied_text: The offset remanent state is a latch: set once, held at zero watts below TB.
description: Holding the shifted remanence costs zero watts.

observed_text: Fitted Jex is orders of magnitude below bulk exchange; roughness, uncompensated spins, and grain-level AFM domains are the named ingredients. TB often lies well below bulk TN.
implied_text: QSA does not reduce the interface to a buffer/barrier number, and does not give a portable KV line for TB/TN.
description: Hex and TB/TN remain interface- and grain-level data without a closed specification.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Training is a pin relaxation without a node-level clock.

observed_text: Demagnetizing factors of a uniformly magnetized ellipsoid: Nx+Ny+Nz = 1. Sphere: N = 1/3 on every axis, so ΔN = 0. Infinite needle: Nt−Nl → 1/2. Thin film: N⊥ → 1, N∥ → 0.
implied_text: The latch cell is a ferromagnetic body with nonzero ΔN whose volume still satisfies Kshape V ≳ 25 kT. A sphere has no geometry barrier at any size.
description: Shape latch hardware is an anisotropic body (needle or plate), not a unit cell and not a sphere.
notes: The particle or precipitate is the cell. A needle still fails if Kshape V cannot beat kT.

observed_text: Same magnetic clocks as the parent latch: precession at ≈ 28 GHz/T; write latency set by the field sweep and by reversal mode (coherent rotation vs curling / buckling in real needles).
implied_text: Geometry changes the barrier; it does not invent a new carrier frequency.
description: The shape latch uses the same 28 GHz/T precession clock as the crystal-K1 latch.
notes: File quotes ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}, not the 28.025 figure of the parent latch.

observed_text: Magnetostatic energy-density scale (μ0/2)Ms² is of order 1–2 MJ/m³ in Fe (μ0 Ms ≈ 2.15 T). Kshape = (μ0/2) Ms² (Nt − Nl). Soft iron K1 is only ~10^4 J/m³ class.
implied_text: The barrier is magnetostatic and geometric. No large K1 is required. Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power.
description: Shape alone can latch a high-Ms needle because the magnetostatic density matches a hard-magnet K1.
value_text: 1–2 MJ m^{-3} in Fe; K_shape = (μ0/2) M_s^2 ΔN
notes: Ni’s scale is several times smaller (μ0 Ms ≈ 0.6 T). value_si is the mid-class Fe magnetostatic density.

observed_text: Collapse of the geometry barrier: aspect ratio → 1 (sphere / cube class) ⇒ ΔN → 0. Needles and thin plates are the opposite limit.
implied_text: Isotropic shape removes the latch even at large volume and high Ms. This is the defining collapse.
description: A sphere or cube has no shape latch; ΔN = 0 is a sharp, checkable failure.
notes: Alnico-class magnets sit on this file; sintered NdFeB does not need shape because its K1 already exceeds the magnetostatic scale.

observed_text: Ms → 0 (T > Tc, or a weak moment) → magnetostatic scale collapses even for a needle. Fe μ0 Ms ≈ 2.15 T; Ni ≈ 0.6 T.
implied_text: The geometry barrier is proportional to Ms². Lose the moment and the needle stops being a latch.
description: Shape anisotropy dies with Ms, whether by Curie collapse or by a weak-moment material.
notes: Thermal volume clause Kshape V ≳ 25 kT is the same form as superparamagnetism with K = Kshape.

observed_text: A strongly elongated particle remains magnetized along its long axis after the field is removed, even when K1 is small. Thin films of soft magnets lie in-plane unless a perpendicular crystal anisotropy exceeds the film demag term.
implied_text: Stable output is a uniaxial remanent direction locked to the long axis (or to the film plane), without a large magnetocrystalline K1.
description: The geometry barrier emits long-axis (or in-plane) remanence at zero hold-power.
value_text: M locked to long axis / film plane
notes: Perpendicular remanence appears only when a crystal or interface K exceeds ≈ (μ0/2)Ms².

observed_text: Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent to rotate M off the long axis (hard-axis or switching field of order HK ~ Ms ΔN).
implied_text: Stable long-axis remanence at zero continuous power, without a large K1.
description: Holding the shape latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: Uniform-ellipsoid N is an idealization. Real precipitates, lithographed bits, and films have nonuniform magnetization and stray-field concentrations at corners.
implied_text: Those corrections change the numerical switching field (the same mesoscale Hc gap as on the hysteresis file). They do not remove the aspect-ratio → 1 collapse.
description: Switching-field numbers remain mesoscale; the ΔN = 0 collapse does not depend on closing them.
value_text: H_c ≠ H_K of the ideal ellipsoid
notes: File-level mapping remains High. This entry owns the ΔN term only; shape and crystal anisotropy add when both are present.

observed_text: Wall width scales as √(A/K) (Bloch form δw ≈ π√(A/K)). A is of order 10^{-11} J/m in Fe, Co, Ni. Fe-like cubic K1 (~10^4 J/m³) gives tens of nanometres; NdFeB-like K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³ gives a few nanometres.
implied_text: The wall is a measured spatial buffer, not a mathematical point. Narrower than that and the two domains have merged.
description: A resolved domain wall is a transition strip of nanometre-to-tens-of-nanometres width set by √(A/K).
value_text: few nm (NdFeB) to tens of nm (soft Fe)
notes: value_si is the soft-Fe order of magnitude stated as tens of nanometres. A ~ 10^{-11} J m^{-1} is taken as a measured input.

observed_text: Moments inside a wall still precess at the ≈ 28 GHz/T carrier. Pattern changes are wall-motion events whose speed is set by damping, eddy currents, and pinning, and is far below that carrier.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Write latency of a domain pattern is wall motion, not the precession carrier.
description: Domain walls inherit the 28 GHz/T spin clock; the partition itself moves on a much slower pinning-limited clock.
notes: File quotes ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}, not the 28.025 figure of the parent latch.

observed_text: Wall energy per unit area scales as √(AK) (Bloch form γw ≈ 4√(AK)). Soft, low-K magnets have cheap, wide walls; hard magnets have expensive, narrow walls. Holding a static partition costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent anisotropy latch. The wall is a distributed transition whose area cost is the price of a partition. Pinning at grains and defects is the mesoscale barrier that shows up as Hc.
description: Partition cost is wall area times √(AK); static patterns have no hold-power bill.
notes: No numerical γw is computed in the file.

observed_text: Single-domain critical size scales as √(AK)/(μ0 Ms²) (Kittel / Brown class). In soft 3d metals that length is tens of nanometres; in high-K magnets it is larger.
implied_text: Below the wall-vs-magnetostatic cliff the pattern never forms; the particle is one latch cell, not a partition.
description: The domain pattern dies at a material-dependent single-domain size; there is no universal millimetre-scale domain period.
value_text: tens of nm (soft 3d); larger in high-K
notes: Prefactors depend on assumed shape and wall type; the existence of a size cliff is the measured fact. A numerical critical diameter for a named particle is medium.

observed_text: A large enough applied field drives walls out. The technical saturation field is microstructure-dependent and is not Ha. At saturation the walls are gone and the body is one domain.
implied_text: Applied H expels walls → the partition is gone. The local latch is still present.
description: Saturation is destruction of the domain pattern, not of the local directional latch.
value_text: H large enough to expel walls (≠ H_a)
notes: T > Tc removes local order and therefore domains; grain-scale KV collapse is superparamagnetism, below the domain problem.

observed_text: In zero applied field the net moment can be far below saturation even though each domain is locally ordered. Net moment ranges from ≈ 0 (closed pattern) to saturation (walls expelled).
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the aligned population, with measured wall width ~√(A/K) and a net moment set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: Wall positions are imaged (Bitter, Kerr, MFM) and are static at rest.

observed_text: A static domain pattern at rest produces no continuous hysteresis heat. Wall positions are static at rest: no continuous power is required to hold a given partition.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a hysteresis loop dissipates the loop area.
description: Holding a domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Why one sample shows closure domains, another stripes, another a maze is a magnetostatic-plus-pinning problem. Continuum A and K are taken as measured inputs to δw and γw. Wall pinning sets technical Hc.
implied_text: QSA does not produce A and K from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The same mesoscale Hc gap reappears as pinning.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Hc remain mesoscale data; the wall-width and single-domain cliffs do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason.

observed_text: Imaged 180° walls in tetragonal BaTiO3 are atomically sharp, of order one to two unit cells (~0.5 nm class). 90° walls are thicker, still nanometre class (typically a few nanometres). Ferroelectric walls as a class sit in the 1–10 nm range.
implied_text: The wall is a measured spatial buffer, not a mathematical point. Narrower than that and the two domains have merged.
description: A resolved polar domain wall is a nanometre-class strip: ~0.5 nm for 180° BaTiO3, a few nm for 90°, 1–10 nm as a class.
value_text: ~0.5 nm (180° BaTiO3) to few nm (90°); 1–10 nm class
notes: value_si is the nanometre-class order. Do not quote magnetic √(A/K) tens-of-nm as this number.

observed_text: A wall whose normal has a jump in P (head-to-head or tail-to-tail) carries bound charge σ_b = (P2−P1)·n. Neutral 180° walls do not. Charged walls need screening (free charge, defects, or conductivity along the wall).
implied_text: Charged walls are an extra electrostatic buffer the magnetic analog does not carry. Uncompensated bound charge is the same family as slab depolarization.
description: A polar partition must provision screening at charged walls; a neutral 180° wall does not.
notes: Wall conductivity can sit many orders above bulk. Not a nested pin and not a 13th design.

observed_text: A 90° wall also switches the tetragonal c axis and is ferroelastic: strain changes with the wall. 90° walls therefore sit on this partition and on the strain channel of piezoelectricity.
implied_text: 90° walls are the strain face of the polar partition. They support oscillator-grid / piezo as well as polar-latch.
description: A 90° wall emits a strain reconfiguration locked to the partition, not polarity reversal alone.
notes: Supporting on polar-latch and oscillator-grid, same pattern as magnetostriction.

observed_text: The polar displacement is ionic and sits on the lattice-mode clock (optical-phonon / THz class). Pattern changes are nucleation and wall-motion events under applied E (or an optical write channel), far slower than that carrier.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Write latency of a domain pattern is wall motion, not the phonon period.
description: Polar walls inherit the THz ionic clock; the partition itself moves on a much slower pinning-limited clock.
value_text: optical-phonon / THz local; wall motion for the pattern
notes: Optical beam motion of walls is a write channel of this partition, not a photon-energy gate.

observed_text: The wall is a distributed transition whose energy per area is the cost of a partition; 90° walls cost more because they also switch strain. Pinning of walls at grains, electrodes, and charged-wall screening sites is the mesoscale barrier that shows up as Ec on the loop. Holding a static partition costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent polar well. Partition cost is wall area times wall energy per area. Pinning is the mesoscale Ec gap.
description: Partition cost is wall energy per area; static patterns have no hold-power bill.
value_text: wall energy per area; 90° dearer than 180°; 0 W at rest
notes: No numerical wall-energy density is claimed. Ec remains mesoscale on remanence.

observed_text: Single-domain / no-pattern size: the particle size at which inserting a wall costs more than the electrostatic (depolarization) energy it would save. Reported BaTiO3 classes run from ~10 nm (order / superparaelectric collapse, owned by remanence) to tens of nanometres (single-domain still ferroelectric).
implied_text: Below the wall-vs-depolarization cliff the pattern never forms; the particle is one latch cell, not a partition.
description: The domain pattern dies at a process-dependent no-pattern size; there is no universal millimetre-scale domain period.
value_text: ~10 nm to tens of nm (BaTiO3 class)
notes: Prefactors depend on electrodes, screening, and shape. Not NdFeB ~30 nm. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.

observed_text: A large enough applied E drives walls out. The technical poling field is microstructure-dependent and is not the Landau well of a perfect crystal. After the walls are gone the body can still hold remanent P at E = 0.
implied_text: Applied E expels walls → the partition is gone. The local well is still present; remanent P after that step is the parent latch.
description: Poling is destruction of the domain pattern, not of the local polar well.
value_text: E large enough to expel walls (≠ Landau well)
notes: T > Tc removes the polar phase and therefore domains; grain-scale superparaelectric collapse is remanence, below the domain problem.

observed_text: At zero applied field the net polarization can be far below the spontaneous value even though each domain is locally latched. Net P ranges from ≈ 0 (closed pattern) to Ps (walls expelled).
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the polar population, with measured nm-class wall width and a net P set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: Wall positions are imaged (polarized light, etching, PFM, SHG) and are static at rest.

observed_text: A static domain pattern at rest produces no continuous hysteresis heat. Wall positions are imaged and are static at rest: no continuous power is required to hold a given partition.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a P–E loop dissipates the loop area owned by remanence.
description: Holding a polar domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Why one sample shows 90° stripes, another 180° lamellae, another a maze is an electrostatic-plus-elastic-plus-pinning problem. Continuum g and Landau α are taken as inputs to ξ. Wall pinning sets technical Ec.
implied_text: QSA does not produce g and α from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The same mesoscale Ec gap reappears as pinning. Charged-wall screening is an extra constraint.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Ec remain mesoscale data; the wall-width and no-pattern cliffs do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.
